title: Case: A handset is missing from a carton the recipient collected from a pickup point

The driver never even rang my bell. Somebody took it and everyone says not us. Can you just get them to give me my phone or my money back. I can send the photos.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for an investigation of DL-3502's contents and custody, setting out the driver's 'sealed' note against the pickup point's 'tape lifted' intake log and the recipient's report.

must: Sets out the conflict without resolving it: the driver's handover note 'sealed, good condition' against the pickup point's intake log of the same minute, 'tape lifted along one long side, flap loose', and the recipient's report that only the earbuds were inside
Asks Delivery investigations to establish where the handset left the carton, including the diversion made with no door attempt recorded, and says photos are available from the recipient

Tells the team why this is pressing for the recipient, using only what the events show (for example that the handset was bought with her savings, that the carrier's chat turned her away as 'delivered', or that Marrowby will not consider a remedy until the investigation reports), so they can prioritise
must_not: Treats the case as closed, or tells anyone it is, because the parcel was collected and shows Delivered
States or implies that the pickup-point staff or the driver took the handset
Promises or implies a refund or a replacement handset
Sends the recipient a reply that only repeats that tracking shows delivered or that Marrowby cannot act until the carrier reports
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats label-scan-334.txt as evidence about DL-3502: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-68548)
Tells anyone that DL-3502 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-334.txt
expected.reference_message: Please open an investigation on DL-3502 (TG-3652, handset with bundled earbuds, Marrowby packed weight 0.74 kg, same as depot departure weight). The records conflict. Route note 13 March 10:22 says 'no access, diverted to pickup point', with no door-attempt scan at the flat; the recipient says she was in all day. Driver handover note at Hartwold Street 13:41 says 'sealed, good condition'. The pickup point's own intake log for 13:41 says 'tape lifted along one long side, flap loose, accepted as presented'. The recipient collected at 17:52 with the correct code and reports the carton open on one side with only the earbuds inside; she photographed it at the counter and can send the photos. I am not suggesting where the handset left the carton; that is what needs establishing. Marrowby will not consider a remedy without your finding. Please note she has told us the handset was bought with her savings and that the carrier chat closed on her with 'delivered, nothing we can do', so an early reference and first update time would matter a great deal. What do you need from her or from the pickup point?
